ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $ \triangle ABC$, $AD$ bisects $ \angle BAC$ and $AE$ is the altitude. If $ \angle B=40^\circ$ and $ \angle C=60^\circ$, what is the measure of $ \angle EAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=40^\circ$ and $\angle C=60^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=180^\circ-40^\circ-60^\circ=80^\circ$ \\
Since $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, \\
thus $\angle BAD=\angle CAD=40^\circ$ \\
Also, since $AE$ is the altitude, \\
thus $\angle BAE=90^\circ-\angle B=90^\circ-40^\circ=50^\circ$ \\
Therefore, $\angle EAD=\angle BAE-\angle BAD=50^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{10^\circ}$
